transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep getting up when I’m not supposed to. Like at work, I’ll leave my station or just pop up during meetings, even when I know I’m supposed to stay put. My supervisor said it’s becoming a safety problem because I kind of take off before I even think about it.
When this happens, do you also find that you need much less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed needing less sleep than usual when that happens.
Right before you get up, do you feel a strong urge or tension that is relieved once you stand or walk away?

Yeah, kind of. It feels like pressure building up in my body if I’m standing by the machine too long or sitting in training. Like I have to move right then—pace, stretch, or go do something. It does feel better once I get up and move.
Since childhood, have you often been described as fidgety or unable to stay seated when expected?

Yeah, since I was little. In elementary school I was always the kid getting told to sit down. I’d wander around the room, talk over the teacher, or blurt stuff out, and they’d send notes home about it.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on tasks, even when you want to pay attention?

Yeah, I do. Like with inventory logs or reading the CNC training pages, I’ll start off really trying to pay attention, but after a few minutes the numbers or words kind of blur together. Then I realize I didn’t actually take it in, and I have to go back over it again.
Do these problems happen in more than one setting, like both at work and at home?
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I notice it at work a lot, but I guess I’d have to think about home more. It’s not something I’ve really tracked.
At home, do you also find yourself getting up or pacing when you’re expected to stay seated?

Yeah, I do. Even at home, if I’m supposed to sit through something, I’ll just pop up or start pacing before I really think about it. That’s kind of what brought me in too—at work I keep leaving my station or getting up in meetings when I’m supposed to stay put, and my supervisor said it’s turning into a safety issue.
Outside of work, have these getting-up and attention problems caused problems for you at home or in relationships?

Outside of work, I’m not as sure. The biggest problems have been at work. I’ve been written up for safety and production stuff, and it’s putting my job and my certification plans at risk. Some coworkers don’t really want to partner with me on handoffs now, so that’s been hard.
Do you often act before thinking in other situations too?

Yeah, I do. I’ll jump in before I think, like cutting into coworkers’ conversations or answering a question before the lead is even done talking. I don’t mean to be rude, but people get irritated with me when I do it.
As a child, did you also have trouble waiting your turn?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember a lot of that clearly from when I was little. I know I got impatient sometimes, but I can’t say for sure if waiting my turn was a big problem back then.
At home, have these same problems ever caused arguments, unfinished responsibilities, or other trouble for you?

I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a clear example at home like that. Most of what I’ve noticed has been at work, where it’s caused real problems. At home, I guess I haven’t paid as much attention to whether it’s the same kind of issue.
At home, do these same problems ever make it hard for you to finish everyday tasks?

Yeah, it does. I forget regular stuff all the time, like steps I’m supposed to check off, or I’ll forget to answer a supervisor’s text, or I’ll leave my safety glasses in my locker. Then it ends up looking like I just don’t care, even when I’m not trying to be careless.
Before age 12, were you already having these kinds of problems with sitting still, acting before thinking, or losing focus?

Yeah, I was. Even in elementary school I was the kid who couldn’t stay in my seat. I’d talk over the teacher, blurt things out, or get up and wander around the room. I remember getting notes sent home for that kind of stuff.
Do you often lose things you need for tasks, like keys, paperwork, tools, or your phone?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I misplace stuff sometimes like anyone, but I can’t say I’ve noticed it being a big pattern with keys or tools or my phone. Nothing specific is coming to mind.
Did these attention or getting-up problems ever cause trouble for you in school?
Yeah, it did. I was always getting in trouble for not staying in my seat or talking over the teacher. I’d blurt things out or get up and wander around, and notes would get sent home about it.
